clauses.reason: A deleted or renamed test cannot pass; its removal in the workspace diff is its accounting.

updates.rationale: Only the workspace's own deletion or rename releases a node, so a node that merely went unreported, or whose file the change did not touch, stays owed.
updates.statement: A failed gate leaves a machine-local failure receipt for its workspace naming first-attempt failed, retry-recovered and runner-reported unreached nodes. Unreached nodes fail their shard. The next gate in that workspace accepts a remembered node that an observation in a change journal the workspace changed names as evidence with its root cause, whatever its shard selection. Otherwise its shard must be selected again, or the gate refuses before running checks, and the node must report passing in that run, unless that shard passes without reporting it, the workspace changed its test file since its base and that file no longer holds its test; such a vanished node is released and its shard's receipt details name it. A retry success never offsets a first failure.

decisions.reason: Perdura's final kept refusing a node its change had deleted or renamed, which no run can ever report passing; it needed a manual root-cause record each time. Releasing only nodes the workspace's own diff removed keeps every other first failure owed.

clauses.reason: Agents name a failing test by its node id; its file is the path evidence.

updates.rationale: Normalizing the two forms agents actually type keeps the stored evidence a path without another evidence kind.
updates.statement: A member or batch workspace may write the journal of an approved change in its tree; a batch write does not claim the change, and final attributes a batch commit that changes only change records to those changes. Resolution evidence is a path in the judged tree or a known validation receipt; the semantic resolve writes a pytest node id as its file path and accepts the record's ID as its target. A deferral needs only its reason; an optional follow-up names an approved change on any local branch and is judged only when written. The final review lists every deferred item under unfinished_work.

clauses.reason: Path contribution alone forgets a member's record once a batch sync brings back identical content.

updates.rationale: Ownership follows who wrote the record, which a later merge of the same content cannot change.
updates.statement: A member's own change packages are those whose change.toml its own first-parent non-merge commits wrote and its base does not hold, in addition to those its contribution paths carry. A synchronization that brings back identical content does not make them inherited; a package that arrives only through a synchronization is not the member's own.

clauses.reason: The requested admission set should survive one conflict.

updates.rationale: Continuation finishes the operation the agent asked for instead of requiring each remaining admission by hand.
updates.statement: When batch-open or batch-admit stops at a merge conflict, the members named after the conflicting one are recorded machine-locally as pending for that batch. The conflict result and status list them; batch-continue commits the resolution and then admits them in order, stopping again at the next conflict with the rest pending.

clauses.reason: Each worktree writes only its own journal files; a repository-wide lock serialized unrelated work.

updates.rationale: The journal files a write reads and appends belong to one worktree; history digests already refuse stale writes.
updates.statement: Journal writes serialize per worktree through a lock in that worktree's Git directory. Writes in other worktrees never wait for it. A writer in the same worktree waits a bounded time for the holder, then refuses naming the active writer.

clauses.reason: Checkouts and branches created outside Signetum need the same confirmed removal as workspaces.

updates.rationale: One confirmed, recorded removal covers every leftover the guard keeps agents from deleting with raw Git.
updates.statement: maintenance workspace-abandon removes a checkout, registered as a workspace or not, that proves neither delivered nor contained, and maintenance branch-abandon removes a local branch without a checkout that the delivery branch does not contain, only when given the exact current tip the owner confirmed, the owner's identity, the confirmation source and a reason; the retirement record keeps them with the tip. maintenance leftovers lists such checkouts and branches read-only. Removal refuses the delivery branch and checkout, open Git operations and staged changes, and discards other uncommitted work only with --discard. These are the only removals for undelivered work; batch-discard is removed.

decisions.reason: Perdura's parallel delivery showed members losing their own change after a batch sync, admissions abandoned after one conflict, unrelated journal writes refused behind one repository-wide lock, node ids refused as evidence and leftovers that only raw Git could remove.

transaction.reason: Apply the approved delivery friction decisions
